title: cost-playbook-generator-and-tiling-presets
author: Asha Patel
description:
Context: Customers frequently ask for prescriptive starting points that balance latency, throughput, and unit cost for new workloads. Our existing recommendations are dispersed across docs, examples, and internal heuristics, which makes onboarding and repeatability hard. This PR introduces an automated Cost Playbook Generator: a small rule-driven engine that synthesizes tiling (batching + prefill) presets and quantization profile suggestions from a workload fingerprint. The output is a human-readable playbook (YAML) and a machine-usable preset that can be consumed by the autoscaler and the optimizer CLI.

What this change does: 1) new package pkg/econ/playbook_generator.go implementing a rule engine that maps workload signals (avg seq len, percentile tail latency, tokens/sec, qps distribution) to a prioritized set of presets; 2) tiling presets declared under cmd/tiling/presets.yaml capturing target batch shapes, max-latency budgets, prefilling thresholds and fallback strategies; 3) quantization profile recommendations in pkg/quant/profiles/defaults.json with compatibility hints for fp16/int8/4bit candidates; 4) a small simulator harness internal/sim that validates presets against synthetic traces and produces estimated unit cost deltas used by the generator; 5) CLI helper scripts (scripts/ci/generate_playbooks.sh) and Python SDK bindings (sdk/python/redwood/econ/playbook.py) to export and apply playbooks; 6) documentation (docs/econ-playbooks.md and website/docs/automation/cost-playbooks.md) and an end-to-end test (tests/e2e/econ_playbook_e2e.go).

Design notes: The playbook is intentionally conservative by default: each suggested preset includes a safety band (latency buffer and a fallback quant profile) to avoid regressions. The rule engine is extensible: new rules are added to pkg/econ/rules.go (single-file today) and unit-tested. The decision path is recorded in the generated YAML under metadata.decision_path to help SRE and customers understand the rationale. We also added telemetry hooks (tools/telemetry/econ-metrics.yaml) to measure playbook adoption and delta to unit cost over the first 48 hours after rollout.

Checklist: - [x] implement generator core and rule set - [x] add tiling presets and quant profiles - [x] add simulator and unit tests - [x] add e2e smoke test - [x] add docs and CLI helpers - [x] CI passes on staging - [x] review and approve by econ + perf reviewers

Commit summary: - feat(econ): add playbook generator and public API surface - feat(tiling): add presets yaml and loader - feat(sim): synthetic workload simulator for validation and scoring - feat(quant): default quant profiles and compatibility hints - feat(sdk): python bindings to generate/apply playbooks - docs: user guide and examples - test: e2e smoke and unit tests for core rules

Files changed (high level): pkg/econ/playbook_generator.go, pkg/econ/rules.go, pkg/quant/profiles/defaults.json, cmd/tiling/presets.yaml, internal/sim/simulator.go, sdk/python/redwood/econ/playbook.py, scripts/ci/generate_playbooks.sh, docs/econ-playbooks.md, website/docs/automation/cost-playbooks.md, tests/e2e/econ_playbook_e2e.go, helm/charts/redwood/values-econ.yaml, tools/telemetry/econ-metrics.yaml.

Review conversation (high-level): Liam Chen: "Solid approach, I like conservative defaults. Please add a small table mapping decision_path nodes to Linear tickets for traceability." Asha (author): "Added mapping field in decision_path and included Linear IDs for the initial ruleset (ENG-2109, ENG-2112)." Sofia Nguyen: "Simulator looks good — can we make synthetic traces configurable by seed so teams can reproduce results?" Asha: "Added seed parameter and deterministic mode in internal/sim, documented in the README." Diego Marquez: "One nit: prefer smaller default batch cap for G5x nodes to avoid GPU OOM with long prefixes." Asha: "Lowered G5x default cap to 128 and added explicit guardrails in presets.yaml."

CI and stability: The PR exercise runs unit tests, linters, and a lightweight e2e on staging. One intermittent flake in the simulator test was debugged and fixed (race on pseudo-random generator). All CI jobs reported green on the final run.

Why this is different: Instead of a single tune-for-cost heuristic, this work produces explainable, versioned playbooks that can be iterated and rolled out safely (canary via rollout policy). It bridges docs, autoscaler configs, and optimizer suggestions into a single artifact that teams can review and apply.

Risks and mitigations: - Risk: a too-aggressive quant suggestion might cause quality regression. Mitigation: every quant recommendation includes a fallback and we added an eval hook so teams can gate rollouts on minimum quality thresholds. - Risk: incorrect presets for niche workloads. Mitigation: playbooks are advisory and require opt-in; the generator includes a confidence score and a "manual review recommended" flag for low-confidence suggestions.

Next steps: - Expose a REST endpoint in the Console to preview playbooks (follow-up PR) - Add a policy compiler that translates playbooks into autoscaler + optimizer rules - Expand the ruleset with tenant-specific historical footprints

Related: ENG-2109 (playbook generator), ENG-2112 (tiling presets canonicalization), internal note: /docs/internal/econ-playbooks-notes.md

Merge outcome: Merged via squash after approvals by Liam, Sofia and Diego.

release_notes: Introduce a Cost Playbook Generator that synthesizes tiling and quantization presets from workload fingerprints. Includes conservative defaults, simulator-backed scoring, SDK bindings, and docs. Playbooks are advisory and include fallbacks to prevent regressions.
notes: This PR is intentionally conservative; follow-up work will add Console preview and per-tenant historical weighting for stronger suggestions. Telemetry will be monitored for 30 days post-rollout to validate unit-econ impact.
